text:
nina cole: morning! having a weird first-week hiccup. ran `docker compose up` and postgres never accepts connections. app logs show `could not connect to server: No such file or directory` and then `dial tcp 127.0.0.1:5432: connect: connection refused`. I'm on mac (M1) using the repo's compose.

nina cole: compose snippet (trim):
```yaml
services:
  web:
    build: .
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:devpass@postgres:5432/app_dev
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14-alpine
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

anya petrov: welcome nina! quick checks: is postgres container actually running? `docker compose ps` and `docker compose logs postgres` will show. Also check if the host folder `./pgdata` contains old WAL files left from another install — that can prevent postgres from initializing on startup.

nina cole: `docker compose ps` shows postgres exited with code 1. logs say `FATAL: database files are incompatible` and lots of 'invalid checkpoint record' messages. ugh.

matt hurley: that usually means the host-mounted data dir has files from a different postgres version or corrupted state. Easiest for dev is to delete the folder and let the container reinitialize: `rm -rf pgdata` then `docker compose up`. If you need the data, try starting postgres with the same version that created the data or copy out the files.

nina cole: I tried removing pgdata and re-up, but now postgres starts then immediately exits with permission denied errors when creating directories under /var/lib/postgresql/data. `chown` from host didn't help because the container runs as uid 999.

anya petrov: common pattern: use `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/data alpine ls -la /data` to inspect ownership without root on host. If you need to chown to the postgres uid: `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/pgdata:/data alpine chown -R 999:999 /data`. That avoids host UID mismatches on mac.

matt hurley: also confirm you're not mounting with osxfs options that enforce root. Another simple approach is to use a named volume instead of host bind in compose for local dev:
```yaml
  postgres:
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  pgdata: {}
```
That sidesteps host permission issues entirely.

nina cole: switched to a named volume and postgres boots fine now, good call. one more odd thing: my app still logs `127.0.0.1` connection attempts even though DATABASE_URL points at `postgres:5432`.

anya petrov: are you running the app on your host or inside the container? 127.0.0.1 implies host-local connection. If you run the binary on host, it will try localhost unless you set env var locally. Inside containers, service names resolve.

nina cole: oops I was launching the binary locally to iterate faster. I changed to `docker compose run --service-ports web sh -c "./start.sh"` and it connects to `postgres` correctly. Thanks!

devops-bot: Reminder: onboarding note 2D prefer named volumes for Postgres on macOS to avoid permission and arch issues. See https://redwood.internal/devenv/postgres for the recommended dev compose snippet.

nina cole: thanks everyone 2D will update the onboarding doc with the named volume tip and note about running the app in-container vs host. saved me a lot of time :heart:
